sonnet.problem: The card spends words explaining the hard word 'Sheol' ('the place of the dead'). That is a gloss the passage doesn't give here, and the dictionary pop-up is meant to handle it.
sonnet.rule: Don't spend card words explaining a hard word. Hard words get a dictionary pop-up (definitions.md, made after the cards).

sonnet.problem: The statement tells the baker what the 'weeping/morning' line means ('sorrow won't last forever and joy is on its way'). The text gives no meaning for this picture. The card also gives away its own answer, because the line is quoted right in the question and the statement just restates it.
sonnet.rule: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect. This includes what a picture means. He retells the picture as the text gives it and says what it stands for only when the passage says so.
